archetype: A Golgari -1/-1 counter aristocrats deck: Hapatra pays you a 1/1 deathtouch Snake for every counter-placement event (one Snake per creature you place counters on, not one per counter), so the deck's removal is also its token engine.

drivers.detail: highest-bracket line present: Hapatra, Vizier of Poisons + Yawgmoth, Thran Physician + Obelisk Spider

engines.how: One -1/-1 counter placement produces a 1/1 deathtouch Snake, one 1/1 Insect per counter, and a 1/1 Elf Warrior — so any of the deck's counter sources becomes three bodies. Parallel Lives doubles all three.

Pay 1 life, sacrifice a Snake to Yawgmoth, put a counter on a creature, draw a card; the counter makes a new Snake and Blood Artist drains. Commander Spellbook lists this at bracket 3, and it is the highest-bracket line the deck contains — the reason the computed floor sits at 3, exactly on target.
Tap Cauldron to give the whole board persist, then sacrifice every creature to Viscera Seer; each one returns with a -1/-1 counter, which is one Snake per creature plus a scry per sacrifice.

Equip Skullclamp to a 1/1 Snake token for one mana; the Snake dies and draws two. Whether the toughness reduction and state-based actions produce the draw before the equip cost is repaid is the part worth resolving.

Massacre Girl gives your creatures wither, so a 1/1 deathtouch Snake's combat damage is a -1/-1 counter rather than damage; when that creature dies with the counter still on it, Necroskitter returns it under your control. Her draw is a separate, narrower trigger that needs the dead creature's toughness to have been less than 1.

Black Sun's Zenith for X puts counters on every creature at once; Obelisk Spider's second ability drains each opponent per creature that receives counters, and Hapatra makes a Snake for each, so the wrath refills your board and closes life totals.

Every end step Gnarlbark draws a card and blights 1; put that counter on a Snake token and the placement makes a replacement Snake while the old one dies to state-based actions, feeding Blood Artist. One card and one Snake per turn cycle, not a loop you can run twice.

gameplan: Shrink the table with counter-based removal while each placement widens your own board, then convert the Snake pile into cards with Skullclamp, Yawgmoth, Erebos, Deadly Dispute and Relic Vial — sacrifice outlets that see tokens — and into life loss with Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat, Bastion of Remembrance and Obelisk Spider, or close with one Triumph of the Hordes infect swing on a wide board.
gaps: Bracket 3 permits at most three Game Changers and I used zero; taking all four in-pool ones (Bolas's Citadel, Demonic Tutor, The One Ring, Vampiric Tutor) would force the floor to 4. Up to three is safe, and the two I would add first are Demonic Tutor and Vampiric Tutor.

Blowfly Infestation is the strongest single card in the pool for this archetype and is excluded solely because Hapatra + Blowfly Infestation is a two-card line with mana_value_needed 0 whose produces names "Infinite death triggers" — that forces the bracket floor to 4. Same reason for Host of the Hereafter.

High Perfect Morcant is excluded on its combo bracket tag alone: High Perfect Morcant + Flourishing Defenses is tagged bracket 4, but its produces list is all "Near-infinite" with no "Infinite" entry, so it is not an infinite by the repo's own test. The exclusion is a bracket-tag decision, not an infinite-combo one. Ivy Lane Denizen is excluded because it forms genuine two-card infinites with Ashnod's Altar, Viscera Seer and Yahenni, all of which I run.

Mana base, resolved this pass: my first plan added eight double-black cards, which crossed the 20% pip quorum, moved black's effective pips to 2 and its source target from 22 to 36 — essentially a mono-black base in a two-colour deck. I fixed it on the spell side rather than the land side, leaving six double-black cards below the quorum. If a future pass wants Phyrexian Arena back, it costs roughly four more dedicated black sources.

Counters put on a permanent as it enters DO count as counters being put on it (CR 122.6). I now apply that consistently: the persist returns and the enters-with-counters bodies are the same case, and I no longer exclude Heirloom Auntie, Bristlebane Battler, Grim Poppet or Wingrattle Scarecrow for a rules reason — they are out on cost and fit.

The one residual rules question, and the stack scenario I want run: Hapatra reads "Whenever *you* put one or more -1/-1 counters on a creature". CR 122.6 settles that entering counters count as being put on; it does not by itself settle who put them when the counter comes from persist or from the creature's own enters-with replacement effect. Resolve that once and it validates or kills four persist slots at a stroke.
Deck-specific protection is missing from the pool. Hapatra's Mark is in-identity but not surfaced; all three protection slots are generic equipment plus Heroic Intervention.

Proliferate density is thin: Contagion Clasp, Contagion Engine and Grim Affliction are all I could find at a reasonable cost. Liliana's Influence and Torment of Venom exist in-identity but ranked out of the pool.
Recursion is 2 slots and I found no strategy section that gives a recursion count — that number is my judgment, uncited. Same for the nine sacrifice outlets.

The blight keyword pays for a trigger with your own creatures' toughness. I found no strategy section on treating your own board's toughness as a resource, so I ran two blight cards rather than the four available.
Forbidden Orchard gives opponents 1/1 Spirits, a real liability against a table with sacrifice outlets — though it also hands you legal targets for -1/-1 counters.
generated_by: manamap pilot build-deck (deterministic; no agent involvement)
keep: Yawgmoth, Thran Physician — the deterministic scorer got this one right and it is the best card in the deck: a free sacrifice outlet, repeatable targeted removal, and a card per activation.
Skullclamp — 1/1 Snakes are the ideal Skullclamp target, and at one mana it is the cheapest card-draw engine in the pool.
Dusk Urchins — it puts a counter on itself every time it attacks or blocks (a Snake each time) and cashes those counters in as cards when it dies.
Erebos, Bleak-Hearted — sacrifice outlet plus draw on a creature that is hard to remove.
Sephiroth, Fabled SOLDIER // Sephiroth, One-Winged Angel — sacrifice-for-a-card on enter and attack, plus a drain on every creature death.
Deadly Dispute — sacrifice a spare Snake for two cards and a Treasure at instant speed.
Solemn Simulacrum — the one baseline ramp card that survives: it fixes, ramps, and draws when it dies to your own sacrifice outlet.
The Meathook Massacre — a scalable wrath that is also a permanent drain engine every time a Snake dies.
Yahenni, Undying Partisan — free sacrifice outlet with indestructible, and it grows off the creatures your -1/-1 removal kills.

Grim Haruspex — morbid draw off every *nontoken* creature that dies, so it converts the persist bodies and sacrificed utility creatures, never a Snake. It is in the deck for the persist package, not the token pile.
The 36-land count. Only one land changed (Haven of the Spirit Dragon out, an eighth Swamp in); after the two double-black cuts the recomputed base clears its targets with no shortfalls.

Six draw-labelled slots against a 10-draw template, deliberately: Yawgmoth, Dusk Urchins and Relic Vial (removal), Deadly Dispute and Solemn Simulacrum (ramp) all draw cards, so the draw *function* count is eleven while only six slots carry the label.

manabase.method: hypergeometric, P(pips by earliest castable turn) >= 90% over 99 cards

notes: Brackets are a conversation, not a calculator — this is the lowest bracket the deck's contents are consistent with, not a verdict.
Tutor density (2) is reported, never scored: WotC removed the tutor restriction on 2025-10-21 and now relies on Game Changers membership, which is already counted above.
Mass land denial is checked against a curated list and is incomplete by construction.

slots.why: Three-mana body that places a counter on ETB and then converts every -1/-1 death into a free land drop from hand or graveyard, which is how the deck keeps hitting six mana.

slots.name: Exemplar of Strength
slots.why: A 4/4 for two that enters putting three counters on one of your own creatures — one Hapatra trigger, and the counters are a resource a persist creature or Channeler Initiate wanted anyway.

slots.name: Festering Mummy
slots.why: One-mana body that puts a counter on any creature when it dies, so it is a Snake on the way in and a Snake on the way out.

slots.name: Flourishing Defenses
slots.why: Third payoff for the same trigger — with Hapatra and Nest of Scarabs out, one Grim Affliction makes three bodies. Also excluded from the scorer by negative embedding similarity.

slots.name: Necropede
slots.why: Two-mana infect body whose damage to creatures is -1/-1 counters, and it places one more counter when it dies.

slots.name: Necroskitter
slots.why: Necroskitter turns your removal into theft: any opponent's creature that dies with a -1/-1 counter on it comes back under your control, and its own wither means blocking it steals the blocker.

slots.name: Nest of Scarabs
slots.why: The single most important non-commander card in the archetype: it doubles every counter placement into an Insect on top of Hapatra's Snake, and the deterministic scorer never found it because its ability embedding scores -0.47 against Hapatra.

slots.name: Obelisk Spider
slots.why: Drains each opponent for 1 every time you put counters on a creature and its combat damage to creatures is itself counter placement — the payoff that turns the engine into a clock without needing an attack step.

slots.name: Parallel Lives
slots.why: Doubles the Snakes, the Insects from Nest of Scarabs and the Elves from Flourishing Defenses; a four-mana enchantment that makes every trigger in the deck twice as large.

slots.name: Plague Belcher
slots.why: A 5/4 menace for three that hands you a Snake on ETB by putting two counters on your own creature — put them on a persist body and you lose nothing.

slots.name: Putrid Goblin

slots.name: Viscera Seer
slots.why: One-mana free sacrifice outlet: it is what turns Cauldron of Souls, the persist package and the drain effects from good cards into an engine.

slots.name: Heroic Intervention
